events.text: Halfway across the river, a storm hits the ferry. The ferryman loses his pole. A mother clutches her baby at the rail.

choices.text: Use your internal energy to steady the boat

ok.log: You plant your feet and push against the current with your palms. The ferry reaches the shore. The mother cries on your shoulder.

fail.log: The ferry capsizes near the bank. Everyone makes it out. You swallow half the river.

ok.log: You swim ashore with the baby held above the water. The ferry makes it too, somehow.

fail.log: The current nearly takes you both. A fisherman pulls you out by the collar.

variants: Midway across the river a storm slams into the ferry. The ferryman loses his pole, and at the rail a mother clutches her baby.

events.text: On a mist-covered peak you find a hut, a teapot already boiling, and two cups. 'You took your time,' says the old woman inside.

effects.log: She talks about nothing: rain, pine needles, a goat she once had. Walking down, you realise every sentence was about martial arts.

choices.text: Ask how she knew you were coming

effects.log: 'I didn't,' she says. 'I always make two cups. Someone always comes.'

events.text: A huge monk sits in the middle of a narrow bridge. 'Toll,' he says. 'One good joke.'

ok.log: He laughs so hard the bridge shakes. He lets you pass and throws in a blessing.

fail.log: Silence. He waits. You tell nine more jokes. Finally he sighs and lets you pass out of pity.

ok.log: You push. He does not move. Then he does, laughing. 'Strong! That also counts.'

fail.log: You bounce off him like a pebble off a mountain. You tell a joke. It is about yourself.

events.text: Locals say the ruined sect on the hill is haunted: every full moon, the sound of swords clashing comes from the empty training ground.

ok.log: At midnight, the wind through the broken halls makes the sound. But the rhythm is a sword form. You learn it from the wind.

fail.log: Cold, fog, and a very aggressive owl. You leave at dawn with nothing but a cold.

effects.log: Some mysteries are better left to the owls.

events.text: A little girl is crying in the busy market. She has lost her father, and she will only say that he 'has a sword and a very big beard'.

ok.log: You find him at the third teahouse, looking frantic. He is the Sect Leader of a small sect, and swears he owes you.

fail.log: It takes all afternoon. You find him eventually. She falls asleep on your shoulder.

effects.log: The guards take her. You hope they are good at finding beards.

events.text: At dawn on the riverbank, you stumble on two masters in the middle of a duel to the death. Neither notices you.

effects.log: You watch the whole duel. The loser falls. The winner turns and looks straight at you, then nods. 'Learn something,' he says.

ok.log: You step between them and talk. Somehow, it works. They share a jug of wine instead. You have made two powerful friends.

fail.log: They both hit you, then go back to fighting. It was worth a try.

events.text: In a town on the southern road, everyone who drinks from the town well falls sick. A Tang family merchant arrived last week.

ok.log: Green tea, charcoal and a root that grows under willows. The town recovers. The merchant is gone.

fail.log: You get sick too, but you get the town to stop drinking. That saves most of them.

ok.log: It was not him: he was framed by a rival. He gives you the antidote and a Tang family token as thanks.

fail.log: He was not the poisoner, and he did not like being accused.

events.text: A blizzard traps you in a mountain pass with a merchant family. Night is coming. The cold is the kind that kills.

choices.text: Warm them all with your internal energy

ok.log: You sit in the middle of the huddle and circulate warmth all night. By morning you are exhausted. Everyone is alive.

fail.log: Your energy is not enough for all of them. You give them your coat, and nearly freeze.

ok.log: A good cave. Warm enough. Everyone lives, and the merchant's children think you are a hero.

fail.log: The cave collapses twice. The third time it holds, just.

events.text: The imperial civil examination is held this year. Passing would make you an official. Most martial artists laugh at the idea.

ok.log: You pass, to the shock of everyone who has seen you fight. The court offers you a post. The murim offers you a raised eyebrow.

fail.log: You fail with honour. The examiner writes 'good calligraphy, strange ideas' on your paper.

effects.log: Swords, not brushes. For now.

events.text: Diving for fish in a deep river pool, you see something glowing among the rocks at the bottom.

ok.log: A river pearl the size of a quail's egg. A jeweller in town nearly faints.

fail.log: You run out of breath and come up choking. The glow is still down there. It will have to wait.

effects.log: The river keeps its secrets. You keep your lungs.

events.text: A young martial artist from another sect has been practising in the same forest clearing as you every morning. Today, she bows and asks for a spar.

choices.text: Spar every morning for a season

effects.log: You learn her style. She learns yours. By autumn you are both better, and friends.

ok.log: You win, narrowly. She bows, grins, and says she will be back stronger.

fail.log: She wins, and shows you exactly how. You say thank you, and mean it.

events.text: Every bookshop in the city is selling 'The Complete Nine Heavens Sword Manual'. The covers are identical. The contents are all different.

ok.log: By reading all three and discarding the nonsense, you piece together something real. Barely.

fail.log: One is a cookbook, one is poetry, one is a map of a city that does not exist. All three are yours now.

effects.log: A wise decision. You feel it in your purse.

events.text: A skinny boy lifts your purse with fingers so quick even you almost miss it. Almost.

choices.text: Catch him and buy him a meal

effects.log: He eats like he has not eaten in days. He hasn't. You leave him with a meal and a lesson in picking the right targets.

choices.text: Catch him and hand him to the guards

effects.log: The guards drag him off. You get your purse back. It feels lighter anyway.

choices.text: Let him go, and keep the rest of your money closer

effects.log: Ten taels. He needed it more. You tell yourself that on the walk home.

events.text: An old retired general at a roadside inn tells you about the war he fought forty years ago, and the one mistake that lost it.

choices.text: Ask what he would do differently

effects.log: He draws the battle on the table in spilled wine. By the time he is done, you understand both war and regret a little better.
He tells you three more stories, each more unlikely than the last. You believe every one.

events.text: Someone has stolen the great bronze bell of the Shaolin Temple. The monks are too peaceful to chase them. The bell is very, very heavy.

ok.log: Twelve exhausted thieves and one bell in a gully. You carry it back up the mountain on your back. The monks ring it in your honour.

fail.log: The thieves are tired but numerous. They escape. The bell stays in the gully until the monks borrow an ox.

effects.log: The monks meditate on the problem. Three days later the thieves bring it back, too frightened by the silence.

events.text: The monsoon traps you in a country inn for a whole month, with nine strangers and one deck of cards.

effects.log: By the end of the month you know everyone's secrets. One of them is a retired assassin. She says you are nice.

choices.text: Train in the stable every day

effects.log: The horses judge you silently. You get stronger anyway.

events.text: A proud young scholar declares that martial artists are brutes who cannot understand the classics, and challenges anyone in the teahouse to prove him wrong.

choices.text: Recite the Art of War from memory

ok.log: You recite all thirteen chapters and add your own commentary. The scholar bows. The teahouse cheers.

fail.log: You get the first chapter right. The rest is mostly improvised. The scholar is smug for a week.

choices.text: Ignore him and drink your tea

effects.log: The tea is excellent. The scholar is not.

events.text: A masked stranger passes you on the road and presses a small wooden box into your hand. 'From someone you once helped,' she says, and is gone.

effects.log: Inside is a stoppered vial of stone milk. You search your memory for who it could be. There are too many possibilities, or none.

events.text: The blacksmith's forge catches fire in the night, and the smith's apprentice is trapped in the loft.

ok.log: You go in through the smoke and come out through the roof with the boy. The smith swears to sharpen your blades for free for the rest of your life.

fail.log: You get the boy out. The fire nearly keeps you.

ok.log: The whole street passes water hand to hand. The boy is pulled out, coughing and alive.

fail.log: The line is too slow. Someone else runs in. The boy lives, barely.

events.text: A man in the market claims to be the legendary master of the Nine Dragon Fist, taking disciples for only 20 taels. He is very clearly not.

effects.log: His 'Nine Dragon Fist' is mostly shouting. The crowd demands refunds. He flees at a very impressive speed.
You learn that the Nine Dragon Fist involves a lot of posing. The poses are, admittedly, very good.

events.text: A widow in a mountain village tells you her husband was a bandit you killed years ago. She is not angry. She wants to know if he died well.

effects.log: You tell her. She nods, thanks you, and pours you tea. You drink it slowly, and think about the road that led you both here.
She smiles for the first time. The lie weighs less than you expected.

events.text: A cave rumoured to hold an old master's treasure turns out to hold about ten thousand bats, all of whom are awake now.

ok.log: Behind the bats: a chest, a small fortune, and a manual on breathing that finally makes sense.

fail.log: Behind the bats: more bats. You leave smelling of them for a week.

effects.log: You run. The bats do not follow. They are very happy where they are.

events.text: On the northern frontier, horsemen raid a border village while the garrison sleeps. You are the only martial artist in town.

ok.log: When the garrison finally wakes, the raiders are gone and you are sitting on the wall, bandaging your hand.

fail.log: The raiders are too many. You buy the villagers time to flee, and nearly pay for it with your life.

ok.log: You run the wall top to bottom, shouting. The garrison drives the raiders off. The captain gives you a horse.

fail.log: The garrison is too slow. The raiders take the grain. No one dies. It is something.

events.text: Something has been eating the rare herbs in the temple garden every night. The monks ask you to keep watch.

effects.log: At midnight, the thief appears: a very old, very fat rabbit who ignores you completely. The monks decide it is a reincarnated abbot and let it be.
You catch the thief: the abbot, sleepwalking. Nobody mentions it again.

events.text: In a pavilion by the lake, a woman plays the guqin so beautifully that a crowd has gathered. When she stops, she looks at you. 'Your turn.'

ok.log: She plays, you recite. By sunset the crowd has doubled and nobody wants to leave.

fail.log: Your poem is enthusiastic. She smiles politely and plays something to cover it.

choices.text: Confess you have no talent for music

effects.log: She laughs and teaches you three notes. You forget two of them. You keep the third forever.

events.text: The silver you received for your last job turns out to be lead painted silver. The man who paid you is still in town.

ok.log: He is drinking your silver away in a teahouse's back room. Correction: he was.

fail.log: He is gone by the time you find his room. So is fifty taels' worth of your pride.

effects.log: The magistrate is sympathetic and useless. You chalk it up to experience.

events.text: A magnificent black horse runs wild in the grasslands. Everyone who tried to ride it has been thrown.

ok.log: Three days of patience and bruises. On the fourth, it lets you ride. It will carry you across the whole murim.

fail.log: It throws you into a bush, then comes back to look at you. You think it is laughing.

effects.log: You watch it run until it is a dot on the horizon. Some things should stay wild.

events.text: You catch a new junior disciple copying the sect's manuals by candlelight. He is a spy, and he is terrified.

effects.log: The elders take him away. You do not ask what happens next.

choices.text: Turn him into a double agent

ok.log: For a year, the rival sect receives beautifully forged manuals full of mistakes. Your elders are delighted when they find out.

fail.log: He runs back to his masters and tells them everything, including your plan.

effects.log: He flees before dawn. He never comes back. You never tell anyone.

events.text: In a village of blacksmiths, an old master offers to forge you a weapon from a fallen star. The price: 200 taels and one year of your time at his bellows.

effects.log: A year of heat and hammering. The blade comes out of the quench humming. It has never been sharpened. It will never need to be.
Your old blade has served you well. It will do.

events.text: A wandering monk asks you to hit him as hard as you can. 'For my training,' he explains, cheerfully.

ok.log: He staggers back one step, beaming. 'Excellent!' He teaches you how he absorbed it. It is the most useful beating you have ever given.

fail.log: Your fist bounces off. Your wrist aches for a week. He thanks you anyway.

effects.log: He finds someone else. You hear the thud from three streets away.

events.text: At night, in the old cemetery, a gang of grave robbers is digging up a famous master's tomb for the manual rumoured to be buried with him.

ok.log: The robbers flee. You refill the grave and burn incense. In the morning, a monk tells you the master's sect will want to thank you.

fail.log: They beat you and escape. The grave is empty. There was never any manual.

choices.text: Wait and see what they find

effects.log: They find a sword, a skeleton and a note: 'You were warned.' They flee screaming. You laugh for an hour.

events.text: Deep in the southern hills, you find a hot spring that the locals say heals old wounds.

effects.log: Old aches you had forgotten about melt away. You leave feeling ten years younger. You are not, but it is nice.
It sells well in the city. It is, as far as you can tell, just warm water. People swear by it.

events.text: An exhausted messenger pigeon lands on your shoulder. The message on its leg is addressed to the Martial Alliance and marked URGENT.

effects.log: It warns of an ambush on the eastern road. You arrive just in time. The Alliance remembers the courier.
It warns of an ambush on the eastern road. You avoid the eastern road for a year.

events.text: A proud swordsman challenges you to a duel on the thin ice of a frozen lake. 'Whoever falls through, loses. Probably forever.'

ok.log: You dance across the ice like a dragonfly on water. He falls through. You pull him out, because you are not a monster.

fail.log: The ice cracks under you. He pulls you out, because neither is he.

effects.log: He calls you a coward. You call him alive. You both walk away.

events.text: In an untouched valley stands a pine tree so old its trunk could hide a house. Martial artists have carved their names into its bark for a thousand years.

effects.log: Your name, beside names from the history books. Someday, someone will read it and wonder who you were.
A thousand years of patience flows down the roots and into you, a little.

events.text: A jade merchant swears his jade pendant 'wards off all martial arts'. He demonstrates by standing still while his assistant 'attacks' him very slowly.

effects.log: He declines, very quickly. The crowd laughs. So do you.
You send it to someone who has it coming, with a note: 'You will need this.' It becomes a legendary murim prank.

events.text: A lady of the imperial court secretly asks you to find her brother, who ran away to join the murim and has not written in three years.

ok.log: You find him running a noodle stall and very happy. He writes to his sister for the first time in years.

fail.log: The trail goes cold. You send her what you learned. She pays you anyway.

effects.log: She understands. The murim and the court do not mix.

events.text: {npc} is gravely ill, and has asked for you by name. Not a friend, not a master: you, {his} old rival.

effects.log: 'I wanted to see who won,' {npc} whispers. You tell {him} it was a draw. {He} laughs until {he} coughs.

mem.note: sent medicine when I was dying

effects.log: You send the best medicine money can buy. {npc} recovers, and writes you a very rude thank-you letter.

events.text: Checking the trading house ledgers, you find that the owner has been cheating the orphanage he claims to support.

effects.log: The scandal is enormous. The owner is ruined; the new owner keeps you on. The orphanage gets its money back, with interest.

ok.log: The orphanage starts receiving the full amount. The owner never notices. You sleep well.

fail.log: He notices. He does not fire you. He just watches you very closely from now on.

effects.log: It is not your business. It feels like your business.

events.text: Your master is away when a wounded swordsman is carried into the clinic. His life is in your hands, and you have only ever stitched a chicken.

ok.log: Your hands shake, then stop shaking. He lives. Your master comes home and says nothing, which is the highest praise.

fail.log: He lives, but only because your master arrives in time. You study every night for a month.

effects.log: Your master arrives in time. 'Next time,' he says, 'you do it.'

events.text: As an inner disciple, you are allowed into the sect's second library. On your first visit, an elder's notes fall from a shelf into your hands.

effects.log: Forty years of one elder's mistakes, corrected in the margins. It saves you years.
The elder raises an eyebrow, then gives them back to you. 'Honest. Good. Read them.'

events.text: At the public bathhouse, two famous masters are arguing about whose scars are more impressive. They turn to you to judge.

effects.log: You pick one. The other challenges you to a duel. You politely decline, in a towel.

ok.log: You tell the story of each scar so well that both masters buy you dinner.

fail.log: Your scars are unimpressive. Both masters are delighted to agree on something.
